messages:
jonathan: Hey all — since yesterday we started seeing intermittent 400s from the embeddings endpoint and large tail latencies (~800ms-1.2s) on some requests. We're on model=v2-embed-small, dynamic batching enabled, max_batch_size=64. Example curl + response attached below. Can someone help triage?

chloe: thanks — can you paste the exact curl and a couple of failing request ids / trace ids? also which region and route?

jonathan: curl: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"v2-embed-small","input":["summary","a longer paragraph..."],"client_id":"client-42"}'
```
Response (one of them): `\{"error":"dimension_mismatch", "expected_dim":1536, "received_dim":0\}`
Trace id: tr_89ab12ef
Region: us-west-2

chloe: dimension_mismatch + 0-length vector is odd. do you have any proxy/ingestion that might alter the payload? also can you share a short span of the batcher debug log around the trace id?

jonathan: no proxy. attaching (redacted) excerpt from our side and the batcher logs we pulled via /internal/debug (paste below).

[customer log snippet]
```
2026-03-17T14:07:10.123Z request tr_89ab12ef received
2026-03-17T14:07:10.124Z enqueue -> route=embeddings priority=normal client_id=client-42
```

[batcher debug from platform]
```
[batcher] 14:07:10.130 assembled_candidates=64 coalesce_ms=120
[batcher] 14:07:10.250 assembled_batch_size=64 wait_time_ms=120 flush_reason=max_batch_size
[slotter] slot_count=8 assignments=[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,64]
[worker-7] received batch id=1732 size=64
[worker-7] model_infer_start batch=1732
[worker-7] model_infer_end batch=1732 duration_ms=1238
[worker-7] per_request: [r0=2ms, r1=2ms, r2=2ms, ... r62=2ms, r63=1200ms]
[model] model_variant=v2-embed-small-quantized fallback=false
[response] id=r63 embedding_len=0  <-- dimension_mismatch
```

matt: thanks for the logs. this is useful. two things jump out: (1) coalesce window=120ms — pretty large, so many small requests are being accumulated and then flushed when max_batch_size triggers; (2) slot_assignments skew: one slot got most of the load (assignments show one slot index with 64), which matches worker-7 handling whole batch and the one request r63 being the tail. that per-request timing (most 2ms, one 1200ms) indicates head-of-line blocking inside the worker or one request doing something expensive (IO, very long input).

lina: also, embedding_len=0 is suspicious — could be the runtime failing to allocate or the model crashing for that particular sub-request and returning an empty vector. we should check model logs for worker-7 around that timestamp. jonathan, can you enable "runtime.model_debug": true on your tenant or provide us a few minutes window and we can pull model worker logs?

jonathan: enabling now. giving a 10m window. also, we observed the error more often when client sends mixed short + very long inputs in the same batch. is that known to cause issues?

chloe: mixed-length inputs should be allowed; the runtime pads/pack sequences. however, if you have extremely long inputs mixed with short ones, it can increase per-batch variance — the long one might take much longer on the model path and cause big tail latency for the rest. when that long request hits an OOM or internal error it could produce an empty embedding  — so two things to try as quick mitigations: (A) reduce max_batch_size to 16 or 32 so large batches are less likely to contain pathological combos, (B) reduce coalesce_window_ms to 10ms so we flush earlier instead of waiting to fill to 64. both are config flags on route-level.

matt: adding to chloe — we recently found a slotting skew edge-case: when max_batch_size is larger than slot_count * typical_worker_capacity and dynamic slot assignment uses a simple round-robin, a single slot can end up receiving many requests if the slot selection logic uses a coarse time bucket. that makes one worker handle a disproportionate amount and exposes any per-request fragility. temporary workaround: set dynbatch.slot_count to 16 or set max_batch_size to a multiple of slot_count. we'll push a fix but for now please try the route overrides.

jonathan: ok trying config change now. setting max_batch_size=32 and coalesce_window_ms=12 and dynbatch.slot_count=16. will run the failing workload for 10 minutes and report back.

[~8 minutes later]

jonathan: quick update — after lowering max_batch_size and increasing slot_count, we still see a few latencies but no 400s so far. tail reduced to ~220-300ms. only one trace id (tr_89ab12ef) previously saw embedding_len=0. thanks.

chloe: great — that's consistent with slot-skew being the main amplifier. for completeness, can you run the small repro loop we use for embedding stress tests and paste the minimal curl script?

matt: repro script (use with care):
```
for i in $(seq 1 600); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"v2-embed-small","input":["short","'"$(python -c \"print('x'*$(( (i%20)*50 )) )\")'"],"client_id":"client-42"}' &
  sleep 0.01
done
```
this floods mixed short+long patterns and usually surfaces the tail. run once with old config, then with new config to compare.

lina: we'll also correlate model worker logs. matt, can you check if worker-7 recorded any OOMs or model runtime exceptions at 14:07:11Z?

matt: yes I pulled the model logs for worker-7: found a single CUDA OOM flagged at 14:07:11. stack trace points to a transient mem spike from one long input packing step; model returned an empty vector for that request before we handled the error gracefully, which the API surfaced as dimension_mismatch. patch queued: ensure per-request OOMs return a proper 5xx and not an embedding_len=0.

chloe: tl;dr and next steps for the customer:
- short-term: set route overrides: max_batch_size=32, coalesce_window_ms=10, dynbatch.slot_count=16.
- repro: run the script matt posted and confirm tail improves.
- we've opened an internal fix: handle per-request OOM so it returns structured 5xx and isolate heavy inputs so they don't bring down batch (WIP).
- if you have latency-sensitive SLAs, consider a dedicated pool for this route or limit max_input_length at the client side.

jonathan: thanks all. applying the changes across 3 services now. please keep me posted on the runtime fix.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: runtime/fix-per-request-oom -> staging (build 4921) by matt — smoke tests running. :rocket:

matt: i'll follow up here once the fix is in canary. for now looks like your config change mitigated both the 400 and the tail spikes. thanks for the quick repro logs.

jonathan: thanks team! :heart:
